title: Proxy-stub Mirroring + Observability Playbook for Local SDK Development
author: Priya Kapoor
body:
Overview

This playbook describes a reproducible local development workflow for Redwood SDK authors and integrators using a lightweight proxy-stub mirroring approach. The goals are: faster iteration, deterministic reproductions of customer issues, integrated observability (traces/metrics/logs), and canonical fixes for common support patterns.

Intended audience

- SDK engineers (Python/Node/Go)
- Developer experience (DX) engineers who maintain sample apps and quickstarts
- Support engineers reproducing customer bugs

When to use this

- Building or changing client-side request shaping, bundling, or streaming logic
- Reproducing flaky streaming behavior reported by customers
- Validating telemetry emitted by SDKs and the local proxy before rolling to CI

What you get out of the box\n
- redwood-proxy (local): a small reverse-proxy that mirrors production request/response shapes and injects deterministic delays or faults
- stub-server: configurable model-response stubs for isolated functional testing
- telemetry-orch: collector that captures spans and metrics locally and forwards to a test telemetry endpoint
- examples for Python and Node SDKs wired to the proxy

Quick architecture (text diagram)

local-dev -> SDK client -> redwood-proxy (mirroring rules + fault injection) -> stub-server or production-mock
                               |\n                               -> telemetry-orch -> local-jaeger / otlp-debug-endpoint

Setup: prerequisites

1) Install Docker (used for stub-server and telemetry collector)
2) Install the local CLI bundle (redwood-local-cli)
3) Node >= 18 or Python >= 3.10 depending on your SDK folder

Quickstart: start everything (3 commands)

1) Start the proxy and stubs

   $ redwood-local-cli start proxy --config ./dev/proxy-config.yaml

   Expected output: "Proxy listening on http://127.0.0.1:8090"

2) Start telemetry collector (OTLP -> local Jaeger)

   $ docker run --rm -p 6831:6831/udp -p 16686:16686 -p 4317:4317 --name otel-local otel/opentelemetry-collector:dev 
     --config=/etc/otel-local/config.yaml

3) Start the stub server with canned responses

   $ docker run --rm -p 8085:8085 -v $(pwd)/dev/stubs:/stubs redwood/stub-server:2027 --dir /stubs

Config reference: proxy-config.yaml (table)

| key | type | example | description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| listen_address | string | 0.0.0.0:8090 | Local bind for developer proxy |
| forward_mode | string | mirror | mirror | forward requests to stub or production variants (mirror|passthrough) |
| mirror_rules | list | see below | Rule set that maps incoming SDK requests to stub behavior |
| fault_injection.delay_ms | int | 0 | Simulated per-request latency |
| metrics_exporter.otlp_endpoint | string | http://localhost:4317 | Where to push spans/metrics |

Example mirror_rules YAML snippet (dev/proxy-config.yaml)

mirror_rules:
  - match:
      path_regex: ^/v1/generate\\b
      method: POST
    action:
      route_to: stub://generation-slow
      inject_delay_ms: 20

SDK wiring examples

Python (requests-based)

1) Set the SDK to use the proxy by environment variable:

   export REDWOOD_API_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8090/v1

2) Run a generation example:

   python examples/generate_text.py --prompt "Write a haiku about compilers"

Node (fetch-based)

1) Start with an .env override in example app:

   REDWOOD_API_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8090/v1

2) Run the example:

   npm run example:generate

Observable signals and where to look

- Traces: open Jaeger at http://localhost:16686 and search for service=redwood-proxy or service=example-client. Look for unusual span durations in the proxy span.
- Metrics: the proxy exports counters: proxy.requests_total, proxy.errors_total, proxy.latency_p50/95. Use Grafana local dashboard (included at http://localhost:3000 with test creds admin/admin).
- Logs: proxy logs are structured JSON in stdout. Key fields: request_id, route, upstream, duration_ms, error_type.

Canonical support issues and fixes (short list)

1) Symptom: Streaming tokens stop after ~1-2s intermittently
   - Cause: Client read timeout at SDK default (Node fetch default socket timeout) + proxy inject_delay_ms simulating network jitter.
   - Fix: Adjust streaming framer in SDK to keep-alive for streaming responses and increase default read timeout; update quickstart's SDK example to set streaming_timeout=30s.

2) Symptom: Embeddings endpoint returns truncated vectors in the stub test
   - Cause: Stub server default max_payload=64KB truncating long vectors when using base64 encoded payloads.
   - Fix: Increase stub-server config max_payload to 256KB in dev/stubs/config.json and add validation to SDK to error earlier.

3) Symptom: Local telemetry shows many "unmapped-route" spans
   - Cause: Proxy mirror_rules didn't match because SDK sent an extra query param (trace_id) in tests.
   - Fix: Add a relaxed path_regex and include a note in the SDK examples to avoid adding extra query params during canonical tests.

End-to-end debugging checklist (ordered)

1) Reproduce: run SDK example against local proxy and confirm the exact failing request body (copy request_id).
2) Capture trace: open Jaeger and filter by request_id; export raw spans if needed.
3) Re-run with increased verbosity: REDWOOD_PROXY_LOG_LEVEL=debug and reproduce.
4) Swap to stub-server vs passthrough to isolate model vs client issue.
4) If flaky: enable fault-injection replay mode in proxy (records deterministic fault seed) and attach the seed to the support ticket.

Sample support ticket template (copy into Zendesk or internal ticketing)

- Title: Repro: streaming truncation (example-app, request_id XXXXX)
- Steps to reproduce:
  1) git checkout <commit>
  2) REDWOOD_API_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8090 npm run example:generate
- Observed behavior: streaming stops after N tokens, proxy span shows duration 1200ms
- Expected behavior: continuous stream until model EOS
- Collected artifacts: jaeger_trace_url, proxy logs (request_id), proxy-config.yaml
- Fault-seed (if used): seed=0x13abf9

Developer check-in guidance (for DX engineers)

- When you change SDK networking behavior (timeouts, retries, streaming frame handling), add a local e2e under /examples/e2e that uses the proxy sandbox and includes one acceptance test that asserts telemetry spans exist for each request.
- Add a canonical-fix note: if a fix affects user-facing defaults (timeouts, buffer sizes), document the change in the SDK CHANGELOG.md and add a quickstart snippet showing the new recommended setting.

Maintenance and ownership

- Proxy binary and mirror-rule schema: owned by platform/dx-proxy team (owners: Priya Kapoor, reviewer: Ethan Miles).
- Stub-server artifacts: owned by sdk-samples team.
- Telemetry-orch: owned by observability team (SLO: 99.9% local-collector health in CI smoke tests).

Backwards compatibility considerations

- Mirror rules should be additive only. Never remove a rule without a migration note and 2-week deprecation in developer examples.
- Defaults that increase resource use (e.g., stub max_payload) must be flagged with the label "devx-resource-impact" and approved by the DX on-call.

Appendix: Useful command snippets

- Dump proxy logs for a request_id:

  $ redwood-local-cli logs --service proxy --filter request_id=abc123 --since 10m

- Run a single e2e test in Python against proxy:

  $ pytest tests/e2e/test_generate.py::test_streaming_against_proxy -k streaming --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8090

Contact and slack channels
